To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) when feature repetitions are eliminated, the congruency sequence effects (CSEs) disappear and (2) when feature repetitions remain, the congruence sequence effects (CSES) increase in the error rates and decrease in the reaction times (RTs).

(1) the congruency effects were reversed, (2) this reversed effect disappeared when feature repetitions were removed from the analysis, and (3) a small but regular congruency effect was found in the error rates in an experiment in which feature repetitions had been eliminated a priori.

(a) cognitive adaptation to response-conflict is not triggered by repetitions of features, and (b) cognitive adaptation is only observed when the conflict is visible, and (c) cognitive adaptation is not observed in error rates.
